ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows triangle XYZ with point P inside. From P, perpendicular segments are drawn to the three sides: PK meets side XY at K with a right-angle mark, PJ meets side YZ at J with a right-angle mark, and PL meets side XZ at L with a right-angle mark. The diagram labels ZP as 20 and ZJ as 12. Thus J is the foot of the perpendicular from P to side YZ, so triangle ZPJ is right at J. Reasoning: In right triangle ZPJ, ZP is the hypotenuse and ZJ is one leg. By the Pythagorean theorem, PJ = sqrt(ZP^2 - ZJ^2) = sqrt(20^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(400 - 144) = sqrt(256) = 16. Since P is the incenter, its perpendicular distances to the sides are equal, so PK = PJ. Therefore PK = 16.
